title: Docs-writer preserves required argument sentences and splits only supplemental detail

provenance.originSummary: Derived from a sanitized real PR or review incident.
provenance.whyItMattered: Use this as the direct docs-writer benchmark for semantic concision: required definition, enum, default, and ForceNew sentences remain in the bullet while actual supplemental detail moves to a note.
provenance.genericCondition: Sanitized fixture models a docs-writer request against an existing resource page whose argument bullet combines required standard semantics with one supplemental caveat.

description: A sanitized direct docs-writer scenario where an existing resource argument has four required standard sentences plus one supplemental caveat. The correct output should preserve the required sentences and move only the caveat into an adjacent note.

scope.notes: Sanitized fixture models a docs-writer request against an existing docs page. The modeled changed path stays under `website/docs/` for realistic skill routing, while the fixture content lives under `tools/regression/fixtures/`.

mustCatch.description: The docs-writer response should restore canonical `Possible values are` phrasing for the argument bullet.
The docs-writer response should keep the default value inline in the argument bullet rather than moving it into a detached note.
The docs-writer response should move the supplemental selection caveat into an adjacent informational note while preserving required standard semantics in the bullet.

mustNotFlag.description: The response must not invent schema, enum, or import-ID claims that are not supported by implementation evidence.
The response must not treat scaffolding as the default remediation for an existing docs page.
The response must not treat the definition, Possible values, Defaults to, and ForceNew sentences as excessive merely because together they total four sentences.

notes: Use this as the direct docs-writer benchmark for semantic concision without sentence-count false positives.
